column1: # Where each woven German plural in lex-de.tsv was read.
# A noun row weaves its second form under an English plural, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. On 2026-10-08 every woven
# German plural was read in the headword line of English Wiktionary's German
# entry for its noun, rendered as a reader sees it, because the raw template
# mostly leaves the plural to Wiktionary's module: {{de-noun|f,^e}} prints
# "Angst f (genitive Angst, plural Ängste)". All 161 are among the plurals
# their own noun's line prints, and none was changed.
# quote is the clause of that line which prints the plural, its qualifiers
# kept, or "invariable" where the line says the plural is the singular. A
# page holds every word of one spelling, so the clause is this word's own
# noun's, of the seed's gender and sense. Nine pages hold another noun of
# this spelling with another plural or none, and each was read by sense:
# Mutter, mother, is "plural Mütter" where Mutter, a nut, is "plural
# Muttern"; Gesicht, face, "plural Gesichter" where Gesicht, a vision, is
# "plural Gesichte"; Lied, song, "Lieder" where an obsolete Lied, member, is
# "Liede"; Tag, day, "Tage" where Tag, a label, is "Tags"; Glas, glass,
# "Gläser or Glas" where the nautical half-hour is "Glasen"; Bauer, farmer,
# "Bauern" where Bauer, a birdcage, is "Bauer"; and Bär, bear, Ort, place,
# tests/tools/plurals.test.ts requires every noun lex-de.tsv weaves in a
# second form to have a line here with that form, citing the noun's own
# entry, its quote printing the form, and fails on a line outliving its row.
